name: All-electric subsea systems
principle: Electric actuators replace hydraulic fluid and its lines, so trees need only power and signals. OneSubsea won a contract for Equinor's Fram Sør, 12 all-electric trees on four templates tied back to Troll C, which Equinor calls the first large-scale all-electric subsea production system.

process_steps.name: Power and signals through electric umbilical

performance.basis: four templates, tieback to Troll C

source.note: Offshore Engineer, Equinor picks OneSubsea all-electric subsea production system for North Sea field
Var Energi release via Cision, Development plan for Fram Sor submitted, 26 June 2025

performance.basis: more than NOK 21 billion (USD 2.2 billion) by the Fram partners; production scheduled to start at the end of 2029

source.note: Var Energi release via Cision, Development plan for Fram Sor submitted, 26 June 2025

reference_plants.name: Equinor Fram Sør all-electric subsea development (North Sea, tieback to Troll C)
reference_plants.capacity: 116 mmboe gross recoverable; four templates with 12 all-electric trees (SLB OneSubsea)
reference_plants.status: PDO submitted and development plan approved 26 June 2025; EPC contract for four templates and 12 all-electric trees awarded to SLB OneSubsea in August 2025; production scheduled to start at the end of 2029, so the first large-scale all-electric system is not yet operating (as of October 2026)

source.note: Var Energi release via Cision, 26 June 2025; EPC award from SLB OneSubsea release via WebWire, 26 August 2025 (read 28 October 2026)

advantages: No hydraulic fluid supply from the host
limitations: First large-scale all-electric subsea production system is still under construction; Fram Sør production is scheduled to start at the end of 2029, so operating experience is not yet available
